findings.summary: The bars have no common origin because the x axis is logarithmic, so a bar's length encodes log(value) rather than value: the 7.6 ms booking bar renders about three quarters as long as the 107.8 ms topology read and nearly as long as the 21.4 ms grey bar, though it is 14 times smaller than the first and 2.8 times smaller than the second. A reader who compares bar lengths instead of reading the printed values misranks the stages. The log axis is a deliberate choice stated in the module docstring, and every bar carries its value, so the figure still reads; a dot or lollipop mark anchored at the target would encode the ratios the prose relies on.

The bar values and the '1 ms target' annotation are drawn at 11 pt, while the data-ink style sheet this script loads sets font.size and the tick label sizes to 14 pt. The numbers therefore render smaller than the tick labels on the same canvas, against the repository rule that a figure uses one text size throughout. Legible at 1400 x 720 px, but inconsistent within one figure and with other figures built from the same sheet.

The x axis is labelled 'wall per stage [ms]', but the grey bar is not a stage: it is the map's wall per solve at batch width 16, a different quantity on the same axis, and it breaks the blue bars' summing property. The caption and the bar's own series label both disambiguate it, so no distinction is lost; the defect is that the axis label alone would mislead a reader who reads the bars without the caption.

The 1 ms target line is drawn in red, where the repository's plotting rules give thresholds and clamps a 1.2 pt dotted neutral grey and reserve red for marks that are past a limit. Every bar here is past the target, so the red reads as consistent with the message rather than wrong, and it does not impede a reader; recorded because the encoding differs from the rule as written and the same script will be reused for figures where not every stage breaches the target.

item_verdicts.contrast: pass — near-black category labels and values sit on a white ground and clear it comfortably; the red target label and dotted line are dark enough to read against white; the grey width-16 bar reads as data rather than fading out.
item_verdicts.data_ink: pass — six solid bars and one-line value labels carry essentially all the ink; there are no gridlines, fills, shading or legend box, and the tick marks and axis rule are the only furniture.
item_verdicts.decoration: pass — white ground, top and right spines removed, no gradient or background wash; the only non-data mark is the dotted 1 ms threshold, which the caption names as the target.
item_verdicts.label_collision: pass — nothing is clipped or overlapping on the 1400 x 720 px render: content sits at least 17 px inside every edge, the longest category label ends left of the axis, each value sits in clear space beyond its bar end, and the target annotation sits above the top bar rather than on it.
item_verdicts.legibility: pass — every category label, bar and printed value reads at a glance from the 735.7 ms Jacobian bar down to the 6.4 ms linear solve without zoom; the smallest printed value, 6.4, is short enough to stay clear of the neighbouring labels on its own row.
item_verdicts.table_form: pass — the figure's message is each stage's distance from a 1 ms target, which is spatial rather than tabular; the same numbers appear in the evidence prose, but the figure does not re-depict a table as an image.
